intro.text: Here Black castles early to prepare a central pawn sacrifice. White either allows the Marshall Attack and defends, or avoids it with an anti-Marshall move that attacks Black's queenside first.
White avoids the Marshall gambit by attacking Black's advanced queenside pawn first. Black must decide how to protect the queenside before the centre opens.
Against the queenside strike Black develops the bishop and invites White to keep the tension. Black gives up the Marshall gambit but gets active pieces in the centre.
Black advances the attacked pawn instead of defending it, gaining queenside space at the cost of a weakened square behind it.

black.text: Black's winners took on bxc3 when White challenged the advanced pawn, opening the b-file for the rook, and put the queen on Qd7.
